niche_preference_profile: This user most often prefers interfaces with strong, explicit visual hierarchy; clear card-based grouping; readable, high-contrast presentation; and either richer visible detail or very deliberate simplification depending on task clarity. They repeatedly favor prominent CTAs, clearly separated sections, rounded containers, and polished, refined layouts. They often like dark navy/high-tech treatments with restrained accent colors, but in several strong cases also prefer light neutral backgrounds when they improve readability and hierarchy. Overall, they prefer structured, polished, easy-to-scan screens with obvious focal points, clear actions, and comfortable spacing over flat, weakly organized, or visually ambiguous layouts.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers a strong focal point and clear prioritization of title, key content, status, pricing, imagery, and primary actions; dislikes weak emphasis, split attention, or flatter hierarchy.
Prefers modular cards, separated sections, outlined or softly bounded content blocks, and clearer grouping of related information; dislikes monolithic panels, flat rows, or poorly separated content.
Prefers open spacing, roomy cards, breathable layouts, and less crowding; dislikes cramped, tightly stacked, or overly dense compositions.
Prefers highly visible primary actions with strong emphasis, clear placement, and explicit labels, often in large rounded buttons; dislikes hidden, weak, or de-emphasized CTAs.

Prefers interfaces with clearly readable text, stronger contrast, and content presentation that is easy to scan and parse; dislikes muted text, low-contrast layouts, or constrained reading experiences.
Prefers softer corner radius, rounded cards/buttons, and a polished, refined finish; dislikes sharper, boxier, rougher, or less finished presentation.

More often prefers richer visible detail, feature-complete cards, explicit labels, segmented controls, and more contextual information when it improves task understanding; only occasionally prefers minimalism when it reduces distraction.
